results.draft_locus: Refunds, Cancels and Chargebacks: Money Flowing Backward ¶2
results.quote: The sequence shows how the Double Refund happened, and where one key would have stopped it.
results.finding: Declared 'example' carrying over 'a refund as a new payment' and introducing 'the Double Refund seen as two such payments'. The sentence carries nothing over from the refund bullets and its subject, 'the sequence', points forward to a figure not yet shown, so the boundary does not express the example relationship.

results.draft_locus: Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits (section opening)
results.quote: | **1 — Starting** (under about €2M) |
results.finding: Declared phrase transition (elaboration) carrying over the four ways to take payments and the four feeds and introducing which setup fits which stage. The section opens directly on the table with no lead-in, so nothing ties the stage rows to the options and feeds just compared.

results.draft_locus: Refunds, Cancels and Chargebacks: Money Flowing Backward ¶2
results.quote: The sequence shows how the Double Refund happened, and where one key would have stopped it.
results.finding: Flow reader A: "'the sequence' refers to the figure that follows, which I only understood after I reached it." The sentence points to Figure 4 before it appears and the incident was last told sections earlier.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 150: "'The sequence' points to a figure that has not appeared yet")

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶7
results.finding: Flow reader A: "'$0.13 + €0.22' mixes currencies, and 'iDEAL costs roughly €0.35' depends on a conversion the text never states. I had to work it out myself." The worked figure needs the dollar-to-euro step stated.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 86: "Mixing dollars and euros without stating a conversion made me stop and check the arithmetic")

results.draft_locus: In Practice ¶4
results.quote: which is why the payout for the sales of 22 April does not equal those sales
results.finding: Flow reader A: "I needed a second read to see that the 22 April batch is the 'later' batch." 'A later payout batch' and 'the payout for the sales of 22 April' are not visibly the same batch.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 218: "I had to work out that the refund issued on 22 April is netted in that day's batch")

results.draft_locus: Strong Customer Authentication and 3-D Secure ¶3
results.quote: One more term matters later. A **merchant-initiated transaction** (MIT) is a charge the merchant triggers later
results.finding: Flow reader A: "The definition lands at the end of a paragraph about liability shift, and the term is next used only in option 3 and in 'When It Goes Wrong'. By then I had forgotten it." The spec places MIT in p25, far from its first use (capture windows, options, expired authorization); the distance comes from the declared order.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 96: "MIT is tacked onto the end of a dense paragraph ... I had forgotten it by the time it came back")

results.draft_locus: Fraud and Card Data: Keep the Attack Out and the Card Number Out ¶6
results.quote: The rules around authentication and fraud are still moving, so the payment design needs someone who tracks them.
results.finding: Flow reader A: "This regulatory outlook is out of place at the end of the card-data section. The Instant Payments point, about a refund rail, has nothing to do with fraud or card scope." Third round with this paragraph flagged in a different place; the difficulty is where the spec puts p26 (and its instant-payments half), not the prose.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 110: "sits inside 'Fraud and Card Data' but is about regulatory change in general ... It is out of place")

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶8
results.quote: One caveat on iDEAL, the chapter's running example.
results.finding: Flow reader A: "'One caveat on iDEAL...' sits after the cost paragraph and feels stranded. It belongs next to the iDEAL row of the methods table." The spec deliberately put p16 after costs (round 1) and rejected merging it into p15; both readers still lose the thread here.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 88: "the iDEAL | Wero caveat is a tangent in the middle of the methods-and-costs discussion")

results.draft_locus: Refunds, Cancels and Chargebacks: Money Flowing Backward ¶4
results.quote: **Chargebacks** are the other backward flow, and not the merchant's decision
results.finding: Flow reader A: "the Waypoint fix (two paragraphs and a figure) sits between the refund bullets and 'Chargebacks are the other backward flow'. The thread about money flowing back is interrupted." The order is the spec's (refunds section problem_solution with chargebacks last; moving them was rejected in round 2).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (line 161: "The section builds to the fix and then restarts with a different backward flow, which feels like an appendix")

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Kestrel & Pine: Three Weeks in January ¶3
results.quote: Most was recovered by asking customers to return it; the bank-transfer refunds could not be recalled.
results.finding: Flow reader A: "It is unclear what 'it' refers to ... the recovery also comes before the table that explains how the incident happened ... 'The dates and details are fictional' is tacked onto the end of an unrelated sentence."

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶2
results.quote: the shopper's bank, the payment scheme and the payment provider do

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Kestrel & Pine: Three Weeks in January ¶1
results.quote: offers iDEAL, cards, PayPal, Klarna, Bancontact and Apple Pay
results.finding: Klarna and Bancontact (and iDEAL in the key-points callout) are named before they are explained; Klarna is glossed as buy-now-pay-later only at the windows paragraph and Bancontact in the country table. Bancontact is on does_not_know.

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶6 (Germany row)
results.quote: "Payment" may be a 30-day receivable or a buy-now-pay-later loan
results.finding: 'Receivable' is on does_not_know and is used here; it is explained only in the Wholesale paragraph of the feeds section.

results.draft_locus: Fraud and Card Data: Keep the Attack Out and the Card Number Out ¶3
results.quote: **PCI DSS** is the card industry's security standard
results.finding: PCI DSS (on does_not_know) is glossed but the acronym is never expanded; AC-6 asks that every acronym be expanded on first use.

results.draft_locus: Introduction callout
results.quote: Payment is a state machine whose truth lives outside your systems.
results.finding: 'State machine' opens the first key point and is never explained; the audience knows APIs, databases and queues, not state machines.

results.draft_locus: Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits ¶1 (Group row)
results.quote: network tokens so saved cards are not locked to one PSP
results.finding: 'Network tokens' and 'a tokenized card base that cannot move' carry the Group-stage argument and are never explained.

results.draft_locus: Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits ¶1 (Growing row)
results.quote: an edge rate limit and a kill switch for guest card payments
results.finding: 'Edge rate limit' is used here and explained only in When It Goes Wrong ('rate limits at the edge of the site').

results.draft_locus: Strong Customer Authentication and 3-D Secure ¶3
results.quote: An exemption buys conversion at the price of fraud liability
results.finding: 'Conversion' (share of checkouts that become payments) is not in already_knows and is never explained, yet carries the exemption trade-off.

results.draft_locus: The Order Depends on a Message It Does Not Control ¶2
results.quote: and every event is signed, because
results.finding: What signing (and later 'owned and verified' endpoints) means is never said; the reader gets only why it matters.

results.draft_locus: The Choices: Four Ways to Take Payments ¶3
results.quote: the PSP's hosted page or drop-in component renders the methods
results.finding: 'Drop-in component' (and 'headless' in option 3, only cross-linked) are not explained, though they distinguish options 2 and 3.

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶2
results.quote: Adyen's, Stripe's and Mollie's documentation
